description: handle_mailbox_set destroy calls query_objects with an inMailbox filter, then get_objects with the returned IDs, then re-filters with email.mailbox_ids.contains_key(&id). The comment says 'correctness safety net for backends that do not support the filter'. But this means: if the backend ignores the inMailbox filter (returns all email IDs), get_objects will fetch ALL emails, consuming unbounded memory. For a large mailbox account this is an OOM vector. A backend author who does not realize filter support is expected will silently expose this. Should enforce a page limit or require the filter be honoured.
title: Mailbox/set destroy: mailbox email cascade fetches all emails, not just that mailbox
